chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I fasted the day of doubt, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan, so should I make it up?' He said: 'No, it is a day for which you were granted success (i.e., your fast is sufficient and valid).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the day of doubt in Sha'ban if it turns out to be Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the fast of the 'day of doubt' (Yawm al-Shakk) as a precautionary measure, declaring it sufficient even if it turns out to be a day of Sha'ban rather than Ramadan. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *ihtiyat* (precaution) in acts of worship, distinguishing it from the specific obligation of Ramadan while affirming the spiritual merit of the fast. The Imam’s phrase 'you were guided to it' highlights the divine acceptance of the worshipper's intention and effort in navigating uncertainty.
